messages.subject: proportional distro unit test pattern
parts:
I wrote some unit tests for the normal distro for proportional-to
probability calcs. The pattern I used below should work for
all the distros and help simplify writing the tests.

The tests are to ensure that the proportionality should
be the same in the full calc (template propto parameter = false)
and the propto calc (template propto parameter = true).

I used a single templated helper function for the normal
distribution and an overloaded equality test function.

I then went through all the combinations of constant and
variable arguments and tested each (holding the constant
part constant and varying the variable part, naturally).

We should be able to reuse the overloaded helper function
expect_eq_diffs, so it should be pulled out into some file
that's included from the other tests.

- Bob

------------------------

using stan::prob::normal_log;
using stan::is_constant;
using stan::agrad::var;

void expect_eq_diffs(double x1, double x2,
double y1, double y2) {
EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(x1-x2,y1-y2);
}

void expect_eq_diffs(var x1, var x2,
var y1, var y2) {
expect_eq_diffs(x1.val(), x2.val(),
y1.val(), y2.val());
}

template <typename T_y, typename T_loc, typename T_scale>
void expect_propto(T_y y1, T_loc mu1, T_scale sigma1,
T_y y2, T_loc mu2, T_scale sigma2) {
expect_eq_diffs(normal_log<false>(y1,mu1,sigma1),
normal_log<false>(y2,mu2,sigma2),
normal_log<true>(y1,mu1,sigma1),
normal_log<true>(y2,mu2,sigma2));
}

TEST(distributionsNormal,propto) {
// d,d,d
expect_propto(1.0,2.0,3.0,
1.0,2.0,3.0);
// d,d,v
expect_propto(1.0,2.0,var(3.0),
1.0,2.0,var(4.0));
// d,v,d
expect_propto(1.0,var(2.0),3.0,
1.0,var(4.0),3.0);
// d,v,v
expect_propto(1.0,var(2.0),var(3.0),
1.0,var(-1.0),var(1.0));
// v,d,d
expect_propto(var(1.0),2.0,3.0,
var(3.0),2.0,3.0);
// v,d,v
expect_propto(var(1.0),2.0,var(3.0),
var(4.0),2.0,var(1.0));
// v,v,d
expect_propto(var(1.0),var(2.0),3.0,
var(2.0),var(-4.0),3.0);
// v,v,v
expect_propto(var(1.0),var(2.0),var(3.0),
var(5.0),var(7.0),var(1.5));
}

- Bob
